lessons.title: Input, output and variables
lessons.summary: Read data in, store it, print it back out.
lessons.notes:
A program runs one line at a time, top to bottom. That order is called **sequence**.

- `input()` reads one line of text typed by the user.
- A **variable** stores a value so you can use it later: `name = input()`.
- `print()` sends a value to the screen.
- Everything `input()` gives you is a **string**. Use `int()` or `float()` to turn it into a number before doing maths.

In OCR exam wording, look for the words *read*, *accept*, *ask the user* (they mean `input()`) and *display*, *output*, *report* (they mean `print()`).
lessons.worked_example:
# Ask for a name and an age, then report back
name = input()
age = int(input())
next_year = age + 1
print(f"{name} will be {next_year} next year")
lessons.worked_example_note: `int(input())` reads a line and converts it to a whole number in one step. The f-string drops the variables straight into the message.

lessons.title: Arithmetic and rounding
lessons.summary: Calculations, integer division and formatting numbers.
lessons.notes:
Python arithmetic operators you need for OCR:

| Operator | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+ - * /` | add, subtract, multiply, divide | `7 / 2` is `3.5` |
| `//` | integer (whole) division | `7 // 2` is `3` |
| `%` | remainder (modulus) | `7 % 2` is `1` |
| `**` | to the power of | `3 ** 2` is `9` |

`round(value, 2)` rounds to 2 decimal places. Watch the difference between `/` (always a decimal) and `//` (drops the decimal part).
lessons.worked_example:
# Convert a number of minutes into hours and minutes
total = int(input())
hours = total // 60
mins = total % 60
print(f"{hours} hours {mins} minutes")
lessons.worked_example_note: `//` and `%` work as a pair: one gives how many whole lots fit, the other gives what is left over.

lessons.title: Exam-style sequencing problems
lessons.summary: Longer scenarios where you decide the steps yourself.
lessons.notes:
Exam questions rarely say "use a variable". They describe a situation and leave you to work out the steps.

A reliable method:
1. Underline every value the program must **read in**.
2. Underline every value it must **output**, and the exact wording.
3. Write the calculation that gets from one to the other.

If the question gives an example of the output, copy the format exactly — spaces, capital letters and units all count.
lessons.worked_example:
# A shop adds 20% VAT to every price.
# Read a price and display the price including VAT to 2 decimal places.
price = float(input())
with_vat = price * 1.2
print(round(with_vat, 2))
lessons.worked_example_note: Adding 20% is the same as multiplying by 1.2. Rounding happens last, after the maths.

tasks.title: Print a message
tasks.brief: Read one line of text and print it back exactly as it was typed.

tasks.title: Double a number
tasks.brief: Read a whole number and print it multiplied by 2.

tasks.title: Add two numbers
tasks.brief: Read two whole numbers on separate lines and print their total.
hints: Call `input()` twice and store each value

tasks.title: Full name
tasks.brief: Read a first name then a surname (two lines). Print them on one line separated by a single space.
hints: An f-string keeps the spacing easy to see

tasks.title: Seconds to minutes
tasks.brief: A stopwatch records a time in seconds. Read the number of seconds and display the whole minutes and the remaining seconds in the form `2 min 30 s`.

tasks.title: Average of three marks
tasks.brief: A teacher records three test marks. Read the three marks (one per line) and display the mean rounded to 1 decimal place.

tasks.title: Change from a note
tasks.brief: A customer pays with a £10 note. Read the cost of the item as a decimal and display the change to 2 decimal places.

tasks.title: Perimeter and area
tasks.brief: Read the width then the height of a rectangle (whole numbers). Display the area on the first line and the perimeter on the second line.

tasks.title: Sponsored walk
tasks.brief: A student is sponsored for a charity walk. Sponsors pay a fixed amount for every complete kilometre walked. The program should accept the distance walked in kilometres (a whole number) followed by the amount paid per kilometre (a decimal), then report the total raised to 2 decimal places.
hints: Read the distance first, then the rate

tasks.title: Cinema booking
tasks.brief: A cinema charges £7.50 per adult ticket and £4.25 per child ticket. Write a program that accepts the number of adults followed by the number of children and outputs the total cost of the booking to 2 decimal places.
hints: Work out each subtotal, then add them
The prices are fixed — no need to read them in

tasks.title: Fuel efficiency
tasks.brief: A driver wants to know how economical a journey was. The program is to take the distance travelled in miles and then the litres of fuel used, both as decimals, and report the miles travelled per litre correct to 2 decimal places.

tasks.title: Packing boxes
tasks.brief: A warehouse packs items into boxes that hold 12 items each. Given the number of items in stock, the program must state how many full boxes can be packed and how many items would be left unpacked, using the format `4 full boxes, 3 left over`.

tasks.title: Sports club membership
tasks.brief:
A sports club is writing software to work out annual membership costs.

Membership costs £25 per month. Members also pay a one-off joining fee of £15.

Write a program that:
- accepts the number of months a new member wishes to join for
- calculates the total amount payable, including the joining fee
- outputs the total in the format `Total: £315`

Assume the total is always a whole number of pounds.
hints: Match the output format exactly, including the £ sign

tasks.title: Temperature conversion utility
tasks.brief:
A weather station stores temperatures in degrees Celsius but its display board works in degrees Fahrenheit.

The conversion is: Fahrenheit = Celsius × 1.8 + 32

Write a program that accepts a temperature in degrees Celsius (which may include a decimal part) and outputs the equivalent temperature in degrees Fahrenheit, correct to 1 decimal place, in the format `21.5C = 70.7F`.
hints: Store the Celsius value so you can print it as well
Round the Fahrenheit value to 1 decimal place

tasks.title: Payroll slip
tasks.brief:
A small business needs a program to produce a simple pay summary.

An employee is paid an hourly rate for the hours they work. Tax of 20% is deducted from the gross pay.

The program must accept the hours worked (a whole number) followed by the hourly rate (a decimal), then output three lines:

```
Gross: 300.0
Tax: 60.0
Net: 240.0
```

All three figures should be rounded to 2 decimal places.

tasks.title: Delivery charge calculator
tasks.brief:
An online shop calculates delivery charges by parcel weight.

The charge is 50p per kilogram, plus a fixed handling fee of £2.99. The shop always rounds the final charge to 2 decimal places.

Design a program that takes the weight of a parcel in kilograms (a decimal value) and displays the delivery charge in the format `Delivery: £5.49`.
hints: Add the handling fee before rounding
